summary: A tunnel to localhost on a VPS you already have: frp exposes a local port on a subdomain you own, Caddy terminates TLS, every tunnel is protected by default, and a local log shows and replays incoming requests. cloudflared does most of this for free; this is for owning the plumbing.

stack.choice: frp (server on the VPS, client locally)
stack.why: a mature reverse proxy, not a hand-rolled TCP forwarder
one certificate for every tunnel name

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Consider cloudflared first
prerequisites.why: Cloudflare Tunnel is free and covers most hobby use with one command. This build is for wanting your own box.

prerequisites.name: A VPS with a public IP
prerequisites.why: The public end of the tunnel.

prerequisites.name: A domain with a wildcard record
prerequisites.why: *.tunnel.yourdomain.com so each tunnel gets a name.
prerequisites.get: Add an A record for *.tunnel pointing at the VPS.
prerequisites.cost: free on a domain you own

prerequisites.name: frp binaries
prerequisites.why: frps on the server, frpc on your machine.
prerequisites.get: Download the release for each platform from github.com/fatedier/frp/releases.

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: FRP_TOKEN
env.where: openssl rand -hex 32; the same value on server and client.

phases.title: The server
phases.goal: frps bound to localhost with a token; Caddy issuing wildcard certificates.

steps.do: Install frps on the VPS with frps.toml bound to 127.0.0.1 and FRP_TOKEN
Caddyfile for *.tunnel.yourdomain.com with the DNS challenge for wildcard certificates
steps.detail: Wildcard certificates need the DNS challenge; Caddy needs a DNS provider module or use per-name certificates on demand.

check: Only 22, 80 and 443 are reachable from outside
A certificate issues for a test subdomain

phases.title: The client
phases.goal: tunnel <port> <name> prints a URL and cleans up on exit.

steps.do: Write a wrapper around frpc that generates a per-tunnel config
Print the URL and remove the route on Ctrl-C

check: A local server on 3000 is reachable at its subdomain over HTTPS

phases.title: Protection

steps.do: Basic auth per tunnel via Caddy, on by default
An IP allowlist flag and an explicit --public flag

check: The allowlist blocks a foreign IP
--public is required to open a tunnel

phases.title: Inspection
phases.goal: See and replay incoming requests locally.

steps.do: Ship Caddy access logs for the tunnel to the client and pretty-print them
A replay command that re-sends the last request body to localhost

check: A webhook appears in the local log within a second

phases.title: Service and README

steps.do: systemd units for frps and Caddy
README with the default-protected rule and the cloudflared alternative

check: The VPS reboots and tunnels resume
The README states the free alternative

phases.title: Operate
phases.goal: Know when the tunnel host is down; keep it patched.

steps.do: Uptime check on the VPS and frps health
Firewall, unattended upgrades, and a rotation procedure for FRP_TOKEN

check: Rotating the token is documented and tested

product.outcome: Tunnels you control, protected by default, with the one free alternative stated honestly.

architecture.swap: Any reverse proxy with wildcard TLS

operations.incident: Rotate FRP_TOKEN; check Caddy logs for unexpected tunnel names.

notIncluded: The global edge, OAuth-in-front with one flag, TCP and TLS tunnels: what ten dollars buys.
after: OAuth in front via Caddy's forward_auth
